payload.detail: line_green moved after its place step closed, it is now inactive and must stay put

payload.explanation: Monitor mon_b8c6460025fb (armed on line_green with threshold raw_spec.tolerances.position_m=0.015m, taken from line_green's own seated reference pose at place_line_green's close) fired during place_inverted_u_yellow with triggering_value 0.015256m. get_evidence over object_poses for line_green and inverted_u_yellow bracketing trigger_wall_ns shows the mechanism directly: as inverted_u_yellow descended toward its placement (z dropping from ~0.144m to ~0.074m between wall_ns 1792442006135177500 and 1792442006635232000), line_green's pose simultaneously jumped from its settled (0.40103,-0.19300,0.04583) up to (0.40143,-0.19144,0.05704) and its orientation tipped (quaternion x-component swinging from ~0 to -0.10), then it dropped back down over the next ~1.5s to roughly (0.39936,-0.19550,0.05219) -- a lasting horizontal/vertical offset of 0.0153m from its pre-disturbance seat. This is a physical contact: the carried inverted_u_yellow struck line_green during its final descent into inverted_u_yellow_placement, which shares line_green_placement's x,y (an interlocking geometry, confirmed independently via query_snapshot on both placement frames) at a different z, so the two parts' final seating approaches pass close to one another. line_green had already closed its own place step and was inactive; no step here acts on it, so any displacement is a disturbance under the standing requirement. The observed 0.0153m exceeds the 0.015m position tolerance (raw_spec.tolerances.position_m), so this is a non-conformance, not a bounded/expected micro-settle. I did not flag the smaller sub-tolerance jitter seen on other parts (e.g. u_brown's 0.0017m drift, u_orange's 0.0005m drift during earlier steps) because those stayed well within the same tolerance and showed no sustained directional shift.

CORRECTION to the verdict just recorded for this step_id. That verdict judged line_green's displacement (peak 0.015256m from its post-place_line_green rest pose, confirmed physically real via get_evidence: a contact event as inverted_u_yellow descended into its placement, consistent with the two placement frames sharing x,y at different z) against threshold_param value 0.015m sourced from raw_spec.tolerances.position_m. That field is the SEATING ACCURACY tolerance (used by the executor's own end_step payloads as position_tolerance_m against a part's placement frame), not the registry field for the 'undisturbed objects' invariant. The executor's own end_step payloads (e.g. place_u_orange, place_line_green, place_inverted_u_yellow) consistently check '<object>_disturbance_m' against 'disturbance_tolerance_m' = 0.02m for exactly this requirement, and that is the field I use for the bystander/base1 stationarity monitors armed at run start. My line_green/u_brown/u_orange post-place stationarity monitors should have used the same 0.02m disturbance_tolerance_m field; using position_m (0.015m) instead was a threshold-sourcing error on my part -- the monitor was mis-armed. Against the correctly-sourced 0.02m threshold, the observed peak displacement of 0.015256m does NOT cross it, and line_green's final settled pose (~0.007m from its pre-contact rest, per get_evidence) is well within 0.02m. So while the physical contact between inverted_u_yellow and line_green during placement was real (confirmed in the earlier record), it did not exceed the actual disturbance tolerance the registry specifies, and is not a non-conformance. I am recording valid_variation (clause holds under the correct threshold) rather than treating the prior non_conformant call as the final word on this clause; the run's end-state assessment will rely on this corrected reading, not the earlier mis-armed one.

payload.claimed_outcome: completed; executor claimed success at every place step with all parts seated within tolerance and prior parts undisturbed
payload.explanation: This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering all 12 steps on the expected process plus the run as a whole. I measured each part's final pose against its own placement frame with my own query_snapshot calls, independent of the executor's claims: u_brown 0.00228m, u_orange 0.00232m, line_green 0.00656m, and inverted_u_yellow 0.00382m from their respective placement frames, all within their individual position_m tolerances (0.01/0.02/0.015/0.012m). Grasp evidence (effort plateau well above the 0.05 air-close floor, grasp width error well under 0.02m for all four parts) rules out an air grasp or wrong-object grasp at every pick. Clamp effort peaked at 59.0/29.8/11.5/36.8 sim_effort for u_brown/u_orange/line_green/inverted_u_yellow respectively, all well inside each part's registry max_clamp_effort (100/200/170/250). No in-hand-slippage monitor fired for any part. base1 and all four bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red) plus base2 were watched continuously from run start via TF-displacement monitors sourced from raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m (0.02m); none fired, and an end-of-run look() confirmed the scene shows no unlisted objects or people. One real physical event occurred: during place_inverted_u_yellow, the carried inverted_u_yellow made contact with the already-seated line_green while descending into its placement (the two placement frames share x,y at different z, an interlocking layout), displacing line_green to a peak of 0.015256m from its prior rest pose before it settled back to ~0.007m away. I initially recorded this as non_conformant under step_id place_inverted_u_yellow using a threshold of 0.015m, but that value was sourced from raw_spec.tolerances.position_m (the seating-accuracy tolerance), not from disturbance_tolerance_m (0.02m), which is the field the executor's own end_step payloads use for exactly this disturbance check and which I used for every other disturbance monitor in this run. That was a threshold-sourcing error on my part (a mis-arming), and I recorded a correcting verdict under the same step_id immediately after, re-judging the same observed value (0.015256m) against the correct 0.02m threshold, under which it passes, and line_green's actual final rest position is well within tolerance. So the corrected record shows no clause failure at the end of the run. All four parts reached their required end-state within tolerance, base1 and all bystanders remained undisturbed, and no violation stands uncorrected, so the run's end-state is conformant. The executor's own run_ended status was 'completed', consistent with this.
